name: George Philip Allen
notable_stories: A Navy airplane mechanic in WWI
He met his second wife, Caroline, while delivering mail on his postal route in San Mateo — she was a chef at a diner he frequented for all his meals
Shortly after World War II he left the family home in Pueblo, Colorado, and moved to San Mateo, California, where he kept delivering mail for the Post Office.
The preparer writes that Esther constantly berated him, and that after his son returned from Japan following WWII he left for work one day and never came back.
He met Caroline at a diner on his mail route where she cooked; as the romance grew he began eating breakfast, lunch and even dinner there.
The preparer remembers him as a gentle man who loved making things; he spent summer visits of about a month in Santa Barbara doing household repairs and teaching the preparer basic woodworking.
milestones: Married Esther Jane Anthony (m. 15 Jun 1919, First Baptist Church, Marceline, MO)
Married Anna Caroline Koenig Winfrey (second marriage)
Worked as a welder and for the ATSF Railroad before starting a career with the US Postal Service
Joined the U.S. Navy, 3 December 1917, St. Louis, Missouri
Died 24 February 1972, Santa Clara, California, aged 74
Joined the US Navy on 3 Dec 1917 in St. Louis
Served in the US Navy in World War I as an airplane mechanic, stationed at Killingholme, England, at one of the first Navy airbases
career: Worked as a welder in the early years, following work around during the Great Depression
Worked for the ATSF Railroad, then for the US Postal Service
